ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, a wooden block A of mass m is placed on a triangular inclined wedge B of mass M. Now horizontal forces of magnitudes $F_{1}$ and $F_{2}$, in opposite directions, are simultaneously used to push wooden block A and inclined wedge B respectively, and they both remain stationary. Then (　　)
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text: The magnitude of the support force exerted by the ground on inclined wedge B must be equal to (M＋m)g

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: In the figure, the triangular inclined wedge B is placed on horizontal ground, and the inclined plane slopes from the lower left to the upper right; wooden block A is placed on the inclined plane of wedge B. On the left side of wooden block A there is a horizontal external force F1 directed to the right, and on the right side of inclined wedge B there is a horizontal external force F2 directed to the left; the two have opposite directions. The problem statement says that both A and B remain stationary. Then reason: Treat wooden block A and inclined wedge B as a whole. For the whole, the support force, friction force, and other interactions between A and B are all internal forces and do not affect the force balance of the whole. Among the external forces on the whole, in the vertical direction there are only the gravitational forces mg and Mg of A and B downward, and the support force N exerted by the ground on inclined wedge B upward. F1 and F2 are both horizontal forces and make no contribution to balance in the vertical direction. Since the whole is stationary, the resultant force in the vertical direction is zero, so N - (M+m)g = 0, giving N = (M+m)g.
